clue.text: Splendid performance in rough stream by oarsman

indicators.note: rough here means roughed up, knocked out of shape, so the letters of stream are rearranged

parts.note: the stroke is the oarsman who sets the rhythm in a rowing eight

explanation.surface: An impressive display of rowing by a crew member battling choppy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns STREAM into MASTER; STROKE is the rower nearest the stern who sets the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliantly clever move or achievement is called a stroke of genius, hence a splendid performance.

clue.text: Furious women altered name on posters

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of name are rearranged

parts.note: ads are advertisements, such as posters

explanation.surface: Angry women complain that a name on the posters was changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges NAME into MAEN, and ADS follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Maenads were frenzied female followers of Bacchus in Greek myth, so wild raging women.

clue.text: The main movement featuring the dandy?

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, and its rolling motion is a long wave or heave

explanation.surface: A question of whether a sea wave features the well-dressed gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is old poetic language for the open sea, not 'the chief'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is the heaving of the sea; it is also old slang for a smart, fashionable man.

clue.text: Turn out a TV tune composed in mid-week

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the letters from the middle of week
mid asks for the central letters of the word week
composed suggests writing music, but here it means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theme tune for television is written in the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges A TV TUNE to VENTUAT; 'mid-week' gives EE, the middle of WEEK, which surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to result or come about, the way things turn out in the end.

clue.text: Wise thinkers, include a Biblical character

indicators.note: include tells you the wanted name is contained within the run of the words wise thinkers

explanation.surface: Wise philosophers are said to include a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The name spans the end of 'Wise' and the start of 'thinkers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is the third son of Adam and Eve in Genesis.

clue.text: Trust new cleaner to come about one

indicators.note: to come about means to surround, so the rearranged letters go round the letter for one
new means remade, so the letters of cleaner are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newly hired cleaner should be trusted when they come round to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLEANER into RELANCE, which goes around I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is dependence or confidence placed in someone, a synonym of trust.

clue.text: Overturnable canoe

indicators.note: overturnable says the word can be turned back to front and still read the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.walkthrough: A canoe can overturn, but here 'Overturnable' means the word reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is an Inuit-style enclosed canoe propelled with a double-bladed paddle.

clue.text: Hurries a temporary resident on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the resident goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel a passenger is on board
a camper stays only a short while at a campsite

explanation.surface: A short-stay passenger dashes about on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention for going inside SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly and lightly, so scampers means dashes or hurries.

clue.text: Valuable pelts ?

parts.note: suggests precious animal furs, but reads as precious gems and also as hurling rocks at someone

explanation.walkthrough: 'pelts' looks like furs but is the verb, to throw things; and 'Valuable' hints at precious gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Gems are called precious stones, and someone who pelts another with rocks stones them.

clue.text: Spirit heater with a number on it

parts.note: the heating element of a kettle or fire is the part that heats
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

explanation.surface: Someone describes a heater, perhaps a gas fire, with a number marked on it.
explanation.walkthrough: L is fifty in Roman numerals, a common way for 'number' to give a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore an elemental is a nature spirit of earth, air, fire or water.

clue.text: Poor Cathy is going on course, perhaps

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of Cathy are disordered

explanation.surface: A girl called Cathy is struggling on a training course or in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges CATHY. 'course' suggests a racecourse or class, but a yacht sails a set course in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing sailing vessel follows a set course of marks, so it is something going on a course.

clue.text: Distributes everything on the square initially

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: Someone hands out everything in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'on the square': O, T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to share out or apportion, so allots means distributes.

clue.text: Shot the examiner, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a good shot is a person who fires accurately
an examiner is a person who marks papers, cryptically a man who marks

explanation.surface: A grim confession: someone gunned down the person setting the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a past-tense verb but is a noun for a skilled shooter; the second sense splits the answer as a person who marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a skilled sharpshooter, called a good shot; an examiner, cryptically, is one who gives marks.

clue.text: Witch-doctor has disturbed island

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of has are moved around

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A tribal healer has been troubling an island community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges HAS into SHA; MAN is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal priest or healer believed to deal with spirits, much like a medicine man.

clue.text: A mother-to be of foreign type in Eliot's work

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
the infinitive to be gives the verb be
de is the French word for of, a foreign of

explanation.surface: An expectant mother of foreign origin appears in a novel by George Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother-to-be' looks like one phrase but splits into DAM (mother) and BE (to be); DE is French for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is George Eliot's first novel, published in 1859.

clue.text: Ruins a drink of tea on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the drink goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel a passenger is on board
cupper is a variant spelling of cuppa, a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Someone spoils things by serving tea on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention for going inside SS (steamship); CUPPER is a variant spelling of the British cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, from sinking a ship deliberately.

clue.text: Looking forward to the Devon trip perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version, so the letters of Devon trip are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is excited about a planned trip to Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DEVON TRIP; Devon is a holiday county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being provident means planning prudently for the future, looking ahead.

clue.text: Soft thing ? Just a little bit

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play softly
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: Someone describes a soft object as only a tiny scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, the musical term for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute fragment or speck, a tiny amount.

clue.text: Something depressing which creates a vacancy for a typist

definitions.text: Something depressing which creates a vacancy for a typist

parts.words: Something depressing which creates a vacancy for a typist
parts.note: reads like a gloomy job loss, but it is the long key a typist presses down to leave a blank between words

explanation.surface: A gloomy event that leaves an office job open for a typist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressing' means pressed down, and the 'vacancy' is a blank space on the page, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key on a keyboard is pressed to insert a blank gap between typed words.

clue.text: Ancient dancer determined to get ahead ?

definitions.text: Ancient dancer determined to get ahead ?

parts.words: Ancient dancer determined to get ahead
parts.note: reads like an ambitious performer, but recalls the Biblical dancer who demanded John the Baptist's head as her reward

explanation.walkthrough: 'get ahead' means win promotion in the surface, but here it is literal: she asked for a severed head on a platter.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodias's daughter danced for Herod and was given John the Baptist's head.

clue.text: Drink for junior clique in R.: A.F. mess?

parts.note: POs are Pilot Officers, the junior commissioned rank in the RAF
a set is a clique, a group of people

explanation.surface: An RAF officers' mess serves a drink to its group of junior members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in R.A.F. mess' tells you the junior people are RAF Pilot Officers (POs), so the junior clique is the POs' set.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset is an old hot drink of milk curdled with wine or ale.

clue.text: Gifts of stories out of part of the Bible

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, so the stories word is placed around the Bible part

parts.note: tales are stories
NT is the New Testament, a part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Gifts in the form of stories taken from a section of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: NT (New Testament) goes inside TALES. The parable of the talents is also in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Free reel — a bit tangled

indicators.note: tangled suggests a reel of line knotted up, so the letters of reel a bit are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frees a fishing reel whose line has got slightly snarled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' rearranges REEL A BIT. 'Free' looks like an adjective describing the reel but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set at liberty, release or emancipate.

clue.text: Fathead appears in part of Corvo

indicators.note: appears in places the letter given by fathead inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
the head, or first letter, of fat is F

explanation.surface: A stupid person turns up in one section of a book by Corvo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fathead' looks like an insult but means the head of 'fat', F. Baron Corvo was the pen name of the writer Frederick Rolfe.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Rolfe wrote as Baron Corvo, so the surname names that author.

clue.text: Motorway girl returned book giving services

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, is read as the letters MI

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for the girl is read backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl comes back along the motorway from a book-signing event.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway, written MI in crosswords; LASS backwards gives SSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the prayers and texts for celebrating Mass, a church service.

clue.text: Battle between chairmen

definitions.meaning: the 1870 Franco-Prussian battle where Napoleon III was captured
a covered chair carried on poles by two bearers, called chairmen, one in front and one behind

explanation.walkthrough: 'chairmen' are not committee heads but the porters who carried an enclosed chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan in France was the site of a famous 1870 battle; a sedan chair was carried between two porters.

clue.text: One bird turns up in a watercourse

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a daw is a jackdaw, a bird

explanation.surface: A lone bird appears in a stream bed.
explanation.walkthrough: I and DAW together read backwards give the answer, as 'turns up' signals in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry river valley in North Africa or Arabia that runs with water after rain.

clue.text: Might be pictured as a way to get money

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
L stands for pound (libra), money

explanation.surface: Being photographed might be a way of earning cash.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or photographer's sitter is one who poses and so is likely to be painted or photographed.

clue.text: Fellow of Cambridge college holds direction of this type

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the direction letter sits inside the college and fellow words

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University
a don is a fellow or tutor of a university college
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A Cambridge don embraces a certain approach to his subject.
explanation.walkthrough: N for north goes between CLARE and DON. 'type' means a printing typeface, not a sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarendon is a bold, slab-serif printing typeface.

clue.text: Order drinks ?

definitions.meaning: a religious order of monks following the Rule of St Benedict
glasses of the herbal liqueur first made by monks at Fecamp

explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a request for drinks, but it is a monastic order.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks of St Benedict's order share their name with a brandy-based liqueur, so both senses fit.
